line_items.description: Miniature Custom Mascot Keychains (Branded with company logo for expo booth giveaway)
Industrial Heavy-Duty Gaffer Tape (Matte Black, 50mm x 50m)
Ultra-low latency USB-C to MIDI Host Interface Adapter for demo station
Collapsible Pop-up Ball Pit Enclosure (1.5m diameter, for interactive product display)

reasoning: Commercial invoice for expo booth goods, evaluated per line under its own category (Ch. 10). Line 0 (mascot keychains, 420.00) and line 3 (ball pit enclosure, 64.50) are event materials under the Ch. 10 event-materials rule: reimbursable only when the note both names the event and states that the budget owner (Department Director, Practice Leader, or equivalent) pre-approved the purchase. The note names the Berlin Indie Games Expo but never states pre-approval, so the second required statement is missing and both lines are deducted in full. Line 1 (gaffer tape, 78.00) is a routine office consumable explicitly listed under the Ch. 10 office-supplies card ('tape'), which caps out-of-pocket consumables at 50.00 per invoice; 50.00 net is reimbursed and the 28.00 excess is deducted. Line 2 (USB-C MIDI adapter, 89.90) is a peripheral with a unit price of 44.95, under the Ch. 10 100.00 peripheral threshold, so it is reimbursable with an itemized invoice and no IT ticket number is required. Line 4: the invoice adds 19% VAT on top of the net subtotal, so per the Ch. 2 calculation steps the VAT is reimbursed only in proportion to the reimbursable net lines: (50.00 + 89.90) x 0.19 = 26.58; the VAT attributable to deducted lines (keychains 79.80, tape excess 5.32, ball pit 12.26 = 97.38) is deducted with them. The buyer company name on the invoice does not affect reimbursability per the Ch. 10 FAQ. The invoice date (2024-03-29, a German public holiday) does not trigger the Ch. 9/13 weekend rules because commercial invoices for goods are never weekend expenses. Total reimbursed: 50.00 + 89.90 + 26.58 = 166.48 of 776.36, so the line is partially approved.
